@copilot Update this PR directly with the same behavior-preserving Gradle cleanup applied to the other suite-owned execution migrations. Consolidate suite declarations and execution configuration into exactly one testing.suites { ... } block per changed build.gradle.kts file, replacing nested testing { suites { ... } } wrappers and separate top-level testing.suites.named(...), testing.suites.withType(...), or testing.suites.executions(...) blocks. Keep custom-suite execution settings inside their registrations where appropriate. Preserve valid suite receiver references when changing the block structure, especially the Cassandra sources.output/classpath expressions. Use only the execution DSL supported by this PR and its existing base; each suite permits only one executions block.

Apply the cleanup to the six builds already changed by this PR: AWS SDK 1.11 javaagent, Cassandra 4.0 and 4.4 javaagent, Couchbase 2.0 javaagent, Pekko HTTP 1.0 javaagent, and Vaadin 14.2 javaagent. Preserve all legacy task names, including registerTask registrations supplied by the existing prerequisite PR #21139. Preserve shaded Cassandra classpaths and pinned driver versions, AWS baseline/latest dependency and suite selection, Vaadin baseline/latest suite selection and build-service constraints, test filters, disablement/JDK gates, metadata profiles, check wiring, and test coverage. Do not replace intentional conditional check dependencies with unconditional all-suite execution.

Inspect related migrated Gradle wiring for further simplification without expanding scope. Scope common task settings to the suites/executions that actually need them, but keep genuinely cross-suite or independent-Test settings in one shared declaration rather than duplicating them in each execution. Verify testLatestDeps system-property consumers in each module and shared test fixtures before removing or narrowing forwarding; Gradle dependency resolution alone does not require that runtime flag. Keep the actual runtime consumers working. Do not alter test behavior merely to simplify configuration.

Preserve the current PR base branch and draft/ready state. Do not edit any other PR, change stack relationships, modify the shared execution DSL, or update agent instructions or conventions documentation. Do not create a new PR. Run narrow formatting and validation in your cloud environment, check both baseline/latest configuration where affected, and verify exact task names, classpaths, settings and lifecycle wiring. Acceptance requires a single testing.suites { ... } block in each of the six builds and behavior-preserving, fully wired executions.

replies.body: Consolidated the six builds to one `testing.suites` block each in `ab968dab`. Preserved the execution names, classpaths, configuration gates, and suite/check wiring. Spotless and baseline/latest task-graph dry-runs passed.

threads.body: [Testing] Calling `executions` adds the suite's default task to `check`, even when no variants are registered (`TestSuiteExecutions.kt:90–98`). This unconditional block therefore adds `vaadinLatestTest` and its Vaadin 24 frontend/Selenium setup to baseline builds; the selected-suite dependency below does not remove it. Guard the whole block with `otelProps.testLatestDeps`, while retaining the build service on the default target for manual baseline runs.

Updated in `853cb983`. The latest suite’s `executions` block is now conditional on `testLatestDeps`; the shared name-scoped service configuration still covers manual baseline `vaadinLatestTest` and both latest tasks. Baseline/latest graphs and service assignments were verified, along with Spotless.

threads.body: [Testing] Removing the single-use Vaadin build service lets `vaadinLatestTest` and `vaadinLatestTestControllerTelemetry` run concurrently and corrupt their shared `~/.vaadin` frontend tooling during installation. The Testcontainers service allows two concurrent tasks, so it does not replace this protection. Restore the name-scoped service wiring for all `vaadinLatestTest*` tasks outside the latest-dependencies condition, preserving protection for manual baseline runs without adding the unselected suite to `check`.

replies.body:
The installation premise no longer applies to these tests. #21047 removed Node/pnpm setup and the pnpm setting. The modern suite is pinned to Vaadin 24.3.13, which uses Flow 24.3.11 and the precompiled development bundle for these standard-component views. [NodeTasks](https://github.com/vaadin/flow/blob/24.3.11/flow-server/src/main/java/com/vaadin/flow/server/frontend/NodeTasks.java) does not schedule npm installation when that bundle can be used.

The follow-up in fffac12b also ran both modern-Vaadin executions concurrently with Node excluded from PATH and confirmed that neither Node installation nor frontend build tools appeared in the shared workspace. The old installation lock is therefore unnecessary for the current test setup; no code change is needed for this finding.
